common: The header keyword is the first statement after front matter, %%{...}%% directives and %% comments; it alone decides the diagram type. Keywords are case-sensitive unless a type's notes say otherwise.
Comments: a whole line starting with %% (indentation allowed). Do not put %% after a statement on the same line: several types read it as text.

Front matter: a YAML block between two --- lines as the very first lines, e.g. ---
title: Orders
config:
  theme: base
  look: handDrawn
---. Keys: title and config (any Mermaid config except the secure ones).
%%{init: {"theme": "forest"}}%% directives are deprecated since 10.5.0 (still read): put configuration in front matter config instead.
accTitle: text and accDescr: text (or accDescr { several lines }) give the drawing an accessible title and description in most types; a type's notes say when it lacks them.

This editor renders with securityLevel strict: HTML in labels is encoded and click callbacks are off. Theme, look (classic, neo, handDrawn) and layout (dagre, elk) are the page's choices unless front matter config sets them.

types.name: Flowchart
types.purpose: Nodes (shapes) joined by edges to show process steps, decisions and dependencies; optional subgraph grouping.
syntax: flowchart LR  - header + optional direction: TB, TD (same as TB), BT, LR, RL; no direction means TB
A  - bare node, label = id

A[Text]  - rectangle; other shapes: A(round) A([stadium]) A[[subroutine]] A[(cylinder)] A((circle)) A(((double circle))) A>asymmetric] A{diamond} A{{hexagon}} A[/lean right/] A[\lean left\] A[/trapezoid\] A[\inv trapezoid/]
A["Text (with) special chars"]  - quote labels containing ( ) [ ] { } | etc.; #quot; #35; #9829; are entity escapes
A["`**bold** _italic_`"]  - markdown string label (backtick inside double quotes)

A@{ shape: cyl, label: "Orders DB" }  - extended shape syntax; shape names lowercase with hyphens (rect, rounded, stadium, fr-rect, cyl, circle, diam, hex, lean-r, lean-l, trap-b, trap-t, dbl-circ, odd, text, doc, docs, delay, h-cyl, lin-cyl, notch-rect, lin-rect, sm-circ, fr-circ, f-circ, fork, hourglass, brace, brace-r, braces, bolt, tri, flip-tri, sl-rect, st-rect, win-pane, div-rect, curv-trap, notch-pent, bow-rect, cross-circ, tag-doc, tag-rect, lin-doc, flag, datastore, folder, bucket, console, browser, person, cloud, bang) plus aliases like process, decision, database, document
A@{ icon: "fa:user", form: circle, label: "User", pos: t, h: 60 }  /  A@{ img: "https://x/y.png", label: "L", w: 60, h: 60, constraint: on }  - icon and image nodes
A --> B --> C  - chaining; A & B --> C & D  - fan-out/fan-in with &
A -->|label| B  or  A -- label --> B  - edge label (dotted: A -. label .-> B, thick: A == label ==> B)
A e1@--> B  then  e1@{ animate: true }  /  e1@{ animation: fast }  /  e1@{ curve: linear }  - edge id + edge metadata
subgraph id [Title] ... end  /  subgraph "Title with spaces" ... end  /  subgraph Title ... end
direction LR  - inside a subgraph sets that subgraph's direction
classDef warn fill:#fee,stroke:#c00  /  class A,B warn  /  A:::warn  /  style A fill:#f9f,stroke:#333
linkStyle 0,2 stroke:#f00  /  linkStyle default interpolate basis  - edge styling by 0-based edge index
click A "https://example.com" "tooltip" _blank  /  click A callbackFn  - interaction (honored only with suitable securityLevel)
A; B --> C  - semicolons can separate statements
relations: -->  arrow;  ---  open line;  -.->  dotted arrow;  -.-  dotted line;  ==>  thick arrow;  ===  thick line;  ~~~  invisible link
--o / --x  circle or cross end;  <-->  o--o  x--x  bidirectional
extra dashes lengthen the edge: --->  ---->  -..->  ===>  (with mid-label, add dashes on the right: A -- No ----> B)
blocks: subgraph id [Title] ... end  - nestable; edges may target a subgraph id; indentation is cosmetic
A@{ ... }  - YAML metadata; may span lines until the closing }
notes: graph and flowchart are equivalent in 12.x (both parse as flowchart-v2); flowchart-elk forces ELK layout. flowchart-v2 is NOT an accepted header keyword.
v12 defaults for flowchart: ELK layout, neo look, redux-color theme; set layout: dagre / look: classic / theme: default in front matter for the old appearance.
A bare lowercase end as a node id breaks parsing (A --> end); use End, END or a different id. end inside a label (A[end]) is fine.
A ---oB or A ---xB makes a circle/cross edge; put a space or capital letter before node ids starting with o or x.
Unquoted labels cannot contain ( ) [ ] { } | or quotes; wrap the label in double quotes. Commas in style values must be escaped as \, (e.g. stroke-dasharray).
@{ shape: ... } names must be lowercase and use hyphens: Rect or manual_file fail with 'No such shape'. Agentflow aliases (task, tool, input, refdoc, action) are not flowchart shapes.
Collapsed subgraph (v11.17+): subgraph needs an id, then id@{ view: collapsed }.
A subgraph's own direction is ignored when any of its nodes link to nodes outside it.
houseStyle: Node text in brackets and double quotes: A["Start"], B("Round"), C{"Decide?"} (lint node-text-quote, auto-fixable).
Node ids only letters, digits and underscores: order_service, not order-service or Bestell Service (lint node-id).
Edge labels in double quotes: A -->|"yes"| B (lint edge-label-quote, auto-fixable).
No special characters in edge labels such as →, <, >, #: write ->, to, vs (lint edge-label-chars).
Subgraph titles with spaces in double quotes: subgraph "Payment Service" (lint subgraph-quote, auto-fixable).
No classDef, style, linkStyle or click unless asked for (lint no-styling, info).
types.example:
flowchart LR
    start(["Start"]) --> check{"Valid?"}
    check -->|"yes"| save@{ shape: cyl, label: "Orders DB" }
    check -->|"no"| fix["Fix input"]
    fix retry@-.-> check
    retry@{ animate: true }
    subgraph svc ["Order service"]
        direction TB
        api["API"] --> worker[["Workers"]]
    end
    save ==> api

types.name: Swimlane
types.purpose: A flowchart split into lanes (top-level subgraphs) to show who owns each step and where work is handed off.
syntax: swimlane-beta LR  - header + optional direction: TB, TD, BT, LR, RL; default TB
subgraph sales [Sales team] ... end  - each TOP-LEVEL subgraph is one lane (id + display label)
subgraph Customer ... end  /  subgraph "Ops team" ... end  - lane without explicit id
lead[Qualify lead]  - node, declared inside the lane that owns it; all flowchart shapes work: A(round) A([stadium]) A{decision} A((circle)) A[(db)] A@{ shape: doc }
lead --> quote  - edge within a lane or across lanes
decide -->|Approved| create  /  decide -- Needs changes --> apply  - labelled edge (label cross-lane handoffs)
classDef attention fill:#fff2cc,stroke:#d6a500  /  class review attention  /  style A fill:#eee
A e1@--> B  /  e1@{ animate: true }  - edge ids and metadata as in flowchart
relations: -->  arrow;  ---  line;  -.->  dotted arrow;  ==>  thick arrow;  ~~~  invisible; --o --x <--> as in flowchart
A -->|text| B  or  A -- text --> B  - label
blocks: subgraph id [Lane label] ... end  - lane; nested subgraphs inside a lane are ordinary groups, not lanes
notes: The -beta suffix is required: swimlane LR is not detected. Available since v11.16.
Same parser/DB/renderer as flowchart (only layout and lane styles differ), so every flowchart statement, shape, edge, classDef/style and the lowercase-end caveat apply unchanged.
The keyword is subgraph, not lane; only top-level subgraphs become lanes.
A node belongs to the first lane (in source order) whose body mentions it, even only inside an edge; declare each node in its own lane and write cross-lane edges after the lanes, outside them.
v12 default look is neo with the redux-color theme (front matter theme: default / look: classic for the old appearance).
types.example:
swimlane-beta LR
    subgraph customer [Customer]
        submit([Submit order])
        confirm[Confirm delivery]
    end
    subgraph store [Store]
        check{In stock?}
        pack[Pack items]
    end
    subgraph carrier [Carrier]
        deliver[Deliver package]
    end
    submit --> check
    check -->|yes| pack --> deliver --> confirm
    check -->|no| submit

types.name: Agent flow
types.purpose: Agentic workflows: agents/flows as containers, tasks, tools, inputs and decisions inside them, and sequence/reference/failure edges between them.
syntax: agentflow-beta TB  - header + optional direction: TB, TD, BT, LR, RL; default TB
id["Label"]@{ shape: task }  - node; agentflow shape aliases: task, tool, input, decision, refdoc, action (any flowchart shape name also works, e.g. cyl, doc)
id[Label]  /  id(Label)  /  id{Q?}  /  id[(DB)]  - flowchart bracket shapes also parse
flow id["Agent name"] ... end  - container (agent/flow); nests; flow id ... end without label is allowed
flow id["Agent"]@{ model: "m", instruction: "..." } ... end  - container metadata inline after the label
global ... end  - nodes declared inside stay at top level even when referenced in flows; takes no id/label/metadata
connector gh["GitHub API"]  then  gh@{ protocol: "http", endpoint: "https://api.github.com" }  - external system
tool@{ shape: tool, connectorRef: "gh.create_issue", params: "city :: String", returns: "Report" }  - binding/contract metadata (free YAML keys are kept)
id@{ view: collapsed }  - collapse a container; id@{ algorithm: "elk.rectpacking" }  - per-container ELK algorithm
fetch@{ shape: tool, retry: 2 }  - metadata; the @{ ... } block may also span several lines (YAML)
a --> b --> c  /  a & b --> c  - chaining and &
a e1@--> b  /  e1@{ animate: true }  - edge id + metadata (curve, animate, animation)
classDef / class / style / linkStyle / click / direction  - same forms as flowchart
relations: -->  sequence (control/data flows to target); longer ---> also accepted
-.-  reference (source consults target; no control passes); -..- also accepted
--x  failure path
a -- label --> b  /  a -- label --x b  /  a -->|label| b  - labels on --> and --x only
blocks: flow id["Label"] ... end  - container, nests to any depth
global ... end  - top-level pinning block, may appear anywhere (even inside a flow)
notes: New in v12; the -beta suffix is required (agentflow alone is not detected).
Only three edge operators exist: -->, -.-, --x. Flowchart edges ==>, -.->, ---, <-->, --o, ~~~ and dotted labels (-. text .-) are syntax errors.
Containers use flow ... end; subgraph is NOT accepted.
Agentflow shape aliases (task, tool, input, decision, refdoc, action) are valid only here; flowchart rejects them.
Unknown shape names fail ('No such shape'); unknown metadata keys are preserved, never rejected. __proto__/constructor/prototype keys are stripped.
%% comments are allowed at the end of a line, not just on their own line.
Defaults: ELK layout, neo look, redux-color theme; own config namespace agentflow (nodeSpacing, rankSpacing, diagramPadding, useMaxWidth, titleTopMargin).

types.name: Sequence
types.purpose: Messages exchanged over time between participants, with activations, notes and control-flow fragments.
syntax: participant A  /  participant A as Alice  - declare (optional; order of declaration = column order)
actor U as User  - stick-figure participant
participant DB@{ "type": "database" } as Orders DB  - stereotype: boundary, control, entity, database, collections, queue; JSON object, alias via as or "alias": "..."
A->>B: text  - message; the colon is required (A->>B: with empty text is ok)
A->>+B: req  /  B-->>-A: resp  - activate target / deactivate source with + / -
activate B  /  deactivate B  - explicit activation
Note right of A: text  /  Note left of A: text  /  Note over A,B: text
create participant C  then a message to C  /  destroy C  then a message to or from C
autonumber  /  autonumber 10 5  /  autonumber off  - sequence numbers (start, step)
title My title  - diagram title
link A: Dashboard @ https://x  /  links A: {"Wiki": "https://y"}  - actor menu
A->>()B: x  /  A()->>B: x  /  A()->>()B: x  - central (lifeline) connections

Message text:
for line breaks; #59; for ';' and #35; for '#'
relations: ->>  solid arrow;  -->>  dotted arrow
->  solid line no head;  -->  dotted line no head
-x  --x  cross (lost/terminated);  -)  --)  open async arrow
<<->>  <<-->>  bidirectional solid/dotted
half arrows: -|\  --|\  -|/  --|/  (top/bottom half);  /|-  \|-  /|--  \|--  (reverse);  -\\  -//  --\\  --//  (stick);  //-  \\-  //--  \\--  (reverse stick)
blocks: loop text ... end
alt cond ... else other ... end
opt cond ... end
par label ... and label ... end  /  par_over label ... and ... end
critical label ... option label ... end
break label ... end
rect rgb(200, 220, 255) ... end  /  rect rgba(0,0,255,.1) ... end  - background highlight; nestable
box Aqua Team name ... participants ... end  - group participants; color first, then label; box transparent Name
notes: Header is case-sensitive (sequenceDiagram); statement keywords are case-insensitive (Note/note, LOOP/loop).
# starts a comment: '#' in message, note or box text truncates the rest of the line, so hex colors (box #f00) do not work; use named colors, rgb() or hsl(), and #35; for a literal #.
; ends a statement, so a semicolon inside message text splits the line; use #59;.
%% comments belong on their own line; after a message colon they become part of the text.
Participant ids may contain spaces (participant Alice Smith) but not : , ; < > or @; use participant X as Long label for display names.
No subgraph, no classDef/class/style statements; styling is via theme/CSS only.
The doc's half-arrow table lists \\- twice; per the grammar \|- is solid reverse bottom half and \\- is solid reverse bottom stick.
types.example:
sequenceDiagram
    autonumber
    actor U as User
    participant API@{ "type": "boundary" } as Public API
    participant DB@{ "type": "database" } as Orders DB
    U->>+API: POST /orders
    API->>DB: insert order
    alt stored
        DB-->>API: id
        API-->>U: 201 Created
    else failure
        DB--xAPI: error
        API-->>U: 500
    end
    Note over U,API: retries allowed
    loop every 5s
        U-)API: poll status
    end
    deactivate API

types.name: ZenUML
types.purpose: Sequence diagrams written like code: participants, async and sync messages, nested calls with { } bodies, fragments (if/else, loops, opt, par, try/catch).
syntax: zenuml  - header; the body is ZenUML, not sequenceDiagram syntax
title Text  - diagram title
Alice  - declares a participant (optional: participants appear in order of first use); one name per line
@Actor Alice  - participant with an annotator: @Actor @Boundary @Control @Database @Entity @EC2 @Lambda @AzureFunction @S3 @SQS @SNS
A as Alice  - alias: A in messages, Alice as the label
<<Interface>> Repo  /  Repo #FF0000  - stereotype; color
@Starter(Alice)  - the participant the first message comes from; write it below the declarations (above one with an annotator or alias, ZenUML draws little or nothing)
// text  - comment; one on the line before a message or fragment is drawn above it (Markdown allowed), others are ignored
relations: Alice->Bob: text  - async message
Bob-->Alice: text  - async reply (dashed)
Bob.method()  /  Bob.method(a, b)  - sync message (from the current participant)
Alice->Bob.method()  - sync message from a named caller
Bob.method() { ... }  - sync message whose body runs inside Bob (nested messages)
new A1  /  new A2(a, b)  - creation message
x = Bob.method()  /  Type x = Bob.method()  - sync message with its reply
return x  - reply from the current method; @return (or @reply) on the line before an async message makes it a reply
blocks: Every block is { ... }, closed by } (there is no end)
if(cond) { } else if(cond) { } else { }  - alt
while(cond) { }  /  for(x) { }  /  forEach(x) { }  /  loop(x) { }  - loop
opt { }  /  par { }  /  critical(text) { }  /  section(text) { }  /  ref(text)  /  group { }
try { } catch { } finally { }  - break
notes: ZenUML is a separate Mermaid plugin (@mermaid-js/mermaid-zenuml 1.0.1), registered by this editor; a page without it cannot draw zenuml.
Its parser takes any text without an error: a mistake draws wrong instead of failing, so check the drawing.
Do not mix in sequenceDiagram syntax: no participant/actor keywords, no ->> or -x arrows, no alt/loop/end, no Note; use the forms above.
Comments are //, not %% (%% lines are dropped by Mermaid before ZenUML reads the source).

types.name: Class
types.purpose: UML class diagrams: classes with members, interfaces, relationships, cardinality and namespaces.
syntax: class Name  |  class Name["Display label"]  |  class `Odd-Name`
class Name { +Type field  +method(arg) Ret }  (members one per line; body may also be on one line)
Name : +Type field  |  Name : +method(arg) Ret  (one member per line, outside a body)
members: visibility + - # ~ ; method = has (); return type after a space; suffix $ static, * abstract
generics with tildes: class Box~T~ , List~int~ items , List~List~int~~ (no commas inside)
A <|-- B  |  A --> B : label  |  A "1" --> "*" B : label (quoted cardinality before/after the arrow)
annotation: class Shape <<interface>>  |  <<interface>> Shape  |  first line inside the { } body
note "text"  |  note for ClassName "text"
direction TB|BT|LR|RL
classDef hot fill:#f96,stroke:#333  |  class Name:::hot  |  cssClass "A,B" hot  |  style Name fill:#f9f
click Name href "url" "tooltip"  |  link Name "url" _blank  |  callback Name "fn"
relations: <|--  inheritance (solid, hollow triangle)
*--  composition (filled diamond)
o--  aggregation (hollow diamond)
-->  association (solid, arrow)
--  link (solid, no head)
..>  dependency (dashed, arrow)
..|>  realization (dashed, hollow triangle)
..  link (dashed, no head)
()--  or  --()  lollipop interface
heads may sit on both ends: A <|--|> B , C *--o D
blocks: class Name { ... } member body
namespace Pkg { class A ... }  |  namespace Pkg["Label"] { }  |  nested namespace blocks  |  dotted namespace A.B { }
notes: Header is case-sensitive: classDiagram (classdiagram is not detected). classDiagram and classDiagram-v2 render identically in 12.x.
Inside a namespace only class declarations, notes and nested namespaces are allowed; write relations outside the namespace block.
A:::style cannot be combined with a relation on the same line (A:::hot --> B fails); style in a separate class line.
Relation labels after ':' cannot contain another ':' or ';'.
Generic type parts are not part of the class name: reference class Box~T~ as Box.
Unquoted class names allow letters, digits, _ , - , . and unicode; use backticks or a ["label"] for spaces or symbols.
Default look in 12.x: neo look, redux-color theme, ELK layout (config can switch back).
types.example:
classDiagram
    direction LR
    namespace Shop {
        class Order {
            +String id
            +List~Item~ items
            +total() Money
            +create(id)$ Order
        }
        class Item["Line Item"]
    }
    class Payable {
        <<interface>>
        +pay(amount) bool
    }
    Customer "1" --> "*" Order : places
    Order "1" *-- "1..*" Item : contains
    Order ..|> Payable
    Account <|-- Customer
    Customer : +String name
    note for Order "Immutable after checkout"
    classDef hot fill:#f96
    class Customer:::hot

types.name: State
types.purpose: State machines: states, transitions, start/end, composite and concurrent states, choice/fork/join.
syntax: StateId  |  StateId : description  |  state "Description with spaces" as StateId
A --> B  |  A --> B : event label
[*] --> First  |  Last --> [*]  (start/end; scoped to the enclosing composite)
state Composite { [*] --> a ... }  |  state "Label" as C { ... }
state c <<choice>>  |  state f <<fork>>  |  state j <<join>>  ([[choice]] [[fork]] [[join]] also accepted)
-- alone on a line inside a composite separates concurrent regions
note right of S : one line  |  note left of S ... end note (multi-line)
direction TB|BT|LR|RL (also inside a composite)
classDef bad fill:#f66  |  class A,B bad  |  A:::bad --> B  |  style A fill:#f00
click A "url" "tooltip"  |  click A href "url"
hide empty description  |  scale 300 width
; may separate statements on one line
relations: -->  transition (the only arrow; no ->, ..>, or labels on both ends)
blocks: state Id { ... } composite state, nestable
note left of|right of Id ... end note
notes: Detection is case-sensitive: stateDiagram / stateDiagram-v2 must be spelled exactly; both use the same v2 renderer in 12.x. Keywords after the header are case-insensitive.
State ids cannot contain spaces, '-', ':' or '{'; use state "Long name" as id. Composite state names must be one word.
Reserved as bare ids: default, click, href, note, state, class, classDef, style.
A '#' at the start of a token begins a comment; inside labels after ':' it is text. Labels cannot contain ';' or '::'.
'--' (concurrency) is only valid inside a composite { }; at top level it is a parse error.
Floating notes (note "text" as N) parse but are not drawn; attach notes with left of / right of.
Transitions between states nested in different composites parse but are not supported by the layout.
classDef styles cannot be applied to [*] start/end states or to composite states.
types.example:
stateDiagram-v2
    direction LR
    [*] --> Idle
    Idle --> Running : start
    state "Running job" as Running {
        [*] --> Fetch
        Fetch --> Build
        Build --> [*]
    }
    state check <<choice>>
    Running --> check
    check --> Done : ok
    check --> Failed : error
    Failed : Retry allowed
    note right of Failed
        Retried up to 3 times
    end note
    Done --> [*]
    classDef bad fill:#f66
    class Failed bad

types.name: Entity relationship
types.purpose: Entity-relationship (data) models: entities with typed attributes and keys, and cardinality-labelled relationships.
syntax: ENTITY  (entity alone)  |  "Name with spaces"
A <card><line><card> B : label  e.g. CUSTOMER ||--o{ ORDER : places
label is mandatory on a relation: one word or "quoted text" (use "" for none)
ENTITY { type name  |  type name PK  |  type name PK, FK "comment" }  one attribute per line
attribute type may end in ? (string? middleName); types/names allow - _ ( ) [ ] . and ~generic~; name may start with *
alias: p[Person] { ... }  |  a["Customer Account"]
subgraph id ... end  |  subgraph id [Title words] ... end  |  subgraph "Quoted id" ... end
direction TB|BT|LR|RL (top level and inside subgraph)
classDef hot fill:#f96  |  class A,B hot  |  A:::hot  |  style A fill:#f00,stroke:#333
word cardinalities: one or zero, zero or one, one or more, one or many, zero or more, zero or many, only one, many(0), many(1), 1, 1+, 0+
word lines: to (identifying), optionally to (non-identifying), e.g. A only one to zero or more B : has
relations: |o / o|  zero or one (left / right side)
|| / ||  exactly one
}o / o{  zero or more
}| / |{  one or more
--  identifying (solid line)
..  or  .-  or  -.  non-identifying (dashed line)
blocks: ENTITY { attributes }
subgraph id [Title] ... end (nestable; can be a relation endpoint by id)
notes: Header is exactly erDiagram (case-sensitive detection); keywords inside are case-insensitive.
A relation without ': label' is a parse error; multi-word labels must be quoted.
Whole-word reserved names fail as entities: one, many, to, end, class, style, classDef, subgraph (prefix use like endpoint is fine).
Keys are only PK, FK, UK (comma-separated); comments are double-quoted and cannot contain '"'.
Entity names allow unicode, letters, digits, _ - * . ; quote names with spaces and refer to them with the same quotes.
Subgraphs (v11.17+) and optional ? types (v11.16+) are newer than many examples online.
Default look in 12.x: neo look, redux-color theme, ELK layout.
types.example:
erDiagram
    direction LR
    CUSTOMER ||--o{ ORDER : places
    ORDER ||--|{ LINE-ITEM : contains
    PRODUCT ||--o{ LINE-ITEM : "ordered in"
    CUSTOMER }|..|{ ADDRESS : "ships to"
    CUSTOMER {
        string id PK
        string name
        string? phone "optional"
    }
    ORDER {
        int id PK
        string customerId FK
        date placedAt
    }
    subgraph catalog [Product Catalog]
        PRODUCT
    end

types.name: Requirement
types.purpose: SysML-style requirement diagrams: requirements, the elements that satisfy or verify them, and typed relationships.
syntax: <reqType> name {  (newline required after '{')
id: 1   text: "..."   risk: low|medium|high   verifymethod: analysis|inspection|test|demonstration  (one per line, all optional)
}  (closing brace on its own line)
reqType: requirement | functionalRequirement | interfaceRequirement | performanceRequirement | physicalRequirement | designConstraint
element name { type: "..."  docRef: "..." }  (same multi-line block rules)
src - <relType> -> dst  e.g. sensor - satisfies -> req1
dst <- <relType> - src  e.g. req1 <- verifies - test1
direction TB|BT|LR|RL
classDef crit fill:#f96  |  class a,b crit  |  a:::crit  |  requirement r:::crit {  |  style r fill:#f00
relations: contains, copies, derives, satisfies, verifies, refines, traces (used as - type -> or <- type -)
blocks: requirement-type name { field lines }
element name { type / docRef lines }
notes: Header must be requirementDiagram followed by a newline; the detector also matches a bare 'requirement' header but the parser rejects it.
Single-line blocks like requirement r { id: 1 } fail: '{' must end the line and each field needs its own line.
All keywords are case-insensitive (verifyMethod = verifymethod, High = high).
Unquoted names/values stop at - < > = : , { and fail if they start with a keyword (test, high, element, text, id, type...); quote them: "my-req", "test the login".
Quoted names are referenced with the same quotes in relations.
An inline 'title ...' line is a parse error; put the title in front matter.
'#' at the start of a token begins a comment.
types.example:
requirementDiagram
    direction LR
    requirement login_req {
        id: 1
        text: "Users can log in with SSO"
        risk: high
        verifymethod: test
    }
    functionalRequirement lockout_req {
        id: "1.1"
        text: "Lock the account after 5 failures"
        risk: medium
        verifymethod: inspection
    }
    element auth_service {
        type: "service"
        docRef: "docs/auth.md"
    }
    lockout_req - derives -> login_req
    auth_service - satisfies -> login_req
    classDef critical fill:#f96
    class login_req critical

types.name: C4
types.purpose: C4-model architecture views (context, container, component, dynamic, deployment) in C4-PlantUML-style macros.
syntax: Person(alias, "Label", "Description")  |  Person_Ext(...)
System(alias, "Label", "Descr")  plus SystemDb, SystemQueue, System_Ext, SystemDb_Ext, SystemQueue_Ext
Container(alias, "Label", "Technology", "Descr")  plus ContainerDb, ContainerQueue and *_Ext variants
Component(alias, "Label", "Technology", "Descr")  plus ComponentDb, ComponentQueue and *_Ext variants
Boundary(alias, "Label", "type") { ... }  |  Enterprise_Boundary | System_Boundary | Container_Boundary (alias, "Label") { ... }
Deployment_Node(alias, "Label", "type", "descr") { ... }  |  Node(...) | Node_L(...) | Node_R(...)
Rel(from, to, "label", "technology")  |  BiRel | Rel_U/Rel_Up | Rel_D/Rel_Down | Rel_L/Rel_Left | Rel_R/Rel_Right | Rel_Back
RelIndex(1, from, to, "label")  (C4Dynamic; index ignored, order of statements numbers the steps)
named args with $: $descr="...", $link="...", $tags="..."; empty positional arg: Container(c, "C", , "descr")
UpdateElementStyle(alias, $bgColor="grey", $fontColor="red", $borderColor="red")
UpdateRelStyle(from, to, $textColor="red", $lineColor="blue", $offsetX="-40", $offsetY="60")
UpdateLayoutConfig($c4ShapeInRow="3", $c4BoundaryInRow="1")
title Text on its own line
relations: Rel = one-way arrow; BiRel = two-way; Rel_U/D/L/R and Rel_Back hint direction
relations reference element/boundary aliases, never labels
blocks: Boundary-type macro (...) { ... } nestable; '{' on the same line or the next line
Deployment_Node / Node / Node_L / Node_R (...) { ... } nestable
notes: Experimental diagram. Macro names and headers are case-sensitive (person(...) or c4context fail); the header must be alone on its first line.

Detector quirk: only C4Context is anchored to the start; the words C4Container, C4Component, C4Dynamic, C4Deployment anywhere in another diagram's text make Mermaid treat it as C4 and fail. Avoid those words in other diagram types.
Not supported: Lay_U/D/L/R, AddElementTag, AddRelTag, RoundedBoxShape and other shape/line helpers, sprites, tags rendering, legend; they cause lexical errors or are ignored.
Unquoted arguments end at ','; quote any text with commas. Quoted text cannot contain '"'.
Layout is not automatic: shapes flow in statement order, c4ShapeInRow (default 4) and c4BoundaryInRow (default 2) per row.
One statement per line; %% comments work, # is not a comment.
Text wraps by default since v11.17.1 (disable with c4.wrap: false).
types.example:
C4Container
    title Container view of the shop
    Person(customer, "Customer", "Buys products")
    System_Ext(pay, "Payment Provider", "Card processing")
    Container_Boundary(shop, "Shop") {
        Container(web, "Web App", "React", "Storefront UI")
        Container(api, "API", "Go", "Business logic")
        ContainerDb(db, "Database", "PostgreSQL", "Orders and products")
    }
    Rel(customer, web, "Uses", "HTTPS")
    Rel(web, api, "Calls", "JSON/HTTPS")
    Rel(api, db, "Reads and writes", "SQL")
    Rel(api, pay, "Charges cards", "HTTPS")
    UpdateRelStyle(api, pay, $lineColor="red", $offsetY="-10")
    UpdateLayoutConfig($c4ShapeInRow="3", $c4BoundaryInRow="1")

types.name: Gantt
types.purpose: Project schedule: tasks as bars on a time axis, grouped into sections, with dependencies and milestones.
syntax: dateFormat <dayjs format>  (input date format, default YYYY-MM-DD; e.g. dateFormat YYYY-MM-DD HH:mm)
axisFormat <d3 time format>  (axis labels, e.g. axisFormat %b %d)
tickInterval <n><millisecond|second|minute|hour|day|week|month>  (e.g. tickInterval 1week)
title <text>  /  section <name>
excludes <weekends|weekday names|YYYY-MM-DD ...>  (repeatable; e.g. excludes weekends 2024-12-25); includes <dates> overrides excludes
weekend friday|saturday  (which days 'weekends' means; default saturday+sunday)
weekday monday..sunday  (week start for week-based tickInterval)
inclusiveEndDates / topAxis  (flags on their own line)
todayMarker off  |  todayMarker stroke-width:5px,stroke:#0f0
<task name> : [tags,] [id,] [start,] end  (e.g. Build : crit, b1, 2024-01-02, 3d)
start = date in dateFormat | after <id> [<id> ...]  (latest end of the listed tasks)
end = date | duration | until <id>  (until = start of that task)
duration = number + ms|s|m|h|d|w|M|y, decimals allowed (1.5d); M is months, m is minutes
tags (must come first, lowercase): active, done, crit, milestone, vert
click <id> href "<url>"  |  click <id> call fn(args)
notes: Detector is /^\s*gantt/ (case-sensitive): Gantt or GANTT is not detected. The rest of the lexer is case-insensitive.
Metadata after ':' is split on ','. 1 item = end (start = previous task end), 2 = start,end, 3 = id,start,end. An id only exists in the 3-item form, so 'Task : t1, 3d' does not set id t1.
Task names cannot contain ':'. Task metadata cannot contain '#' or ';' (';' is a parse error).

A task line whose name starts with a keyword plus space (title, section, excludes, includes, dateFormat, axisFormat, click, ...) is silently taken as that statement; e.g. 'Title page : 1d' becomes the chart title.
Unknown ids in after/until and invalid durations only log a warning: the task falls back to today or zero length, so typos render wrong rather than fail.
Milestones need an id and a duration to be referenceable: Release : milestone, m1, 2024-02-01, 0d.
vert draws a full-height vertical marker and takes no row; the docs' tag list omits it, but ganttDb accepts it.
displayMode: compact (several tasks per row) is config only (frontmatter gantt.displayMode), not a statement.
types.example:
gantt
    title Release plan
    dateFormat YYYY-MM-DD
    axisFormat %b %d
    excludes weekends
    section Build
    Design      : done, des, 2024-01-02, 3d
    Implement   : active, impl, after des, 5d
    section Ship
    Test        : crit, test, after impl, 2d
    Release     : milestone, rel, after test, 0d
    Code freeze : vert, cf, 2024-01-12, 0d

types.name: Pie
types.purpose: Proportions of a whole: one slice per labeled numeric value.
syntax: pie [showData] [title <text>]  (e.g. pie showData title Pets; showData appends values to legend)
title <text>  (alternatively on its own line after pie)
"<label>" : <number>  (e.g. "Dogs" : 386; one slice per line)
label: double- or single-quoted string, required
number: integer or decimal with digits on both sides of '.' (42, 42.5)
notes: Detector is /^\s*pie/ and keywords are case-sensitive: Pie is not detected, showdata is not accepted.
Labels must be quoted; Dogs : 5 is a lexer error.
Negative values throw an error. 0 is accepted (the docs say values must be > 0), but slices under 1% are not drawn.
.5, 5., 1e3, 1,000 and leading-zero integers like 05 are not valid numbers.
Duplicate labels: only the first one is kept.
Slices are drawn in source order. donutHole, legendPosition, highlightSlice and textPosition are config (pie.*), not statements.
types.example:
pie showData
    title Key elements in Product X
    "Calcium" : 42.96
    "Potassium" : 50.05
    "Magnesium" : 10.01
    "Iron" : 5

types.name: User journey
types.purpose: Steps a user takes to complete a goal, grouped in sections, each scored for satisfaction and tagged with actors.
syntax: title <text>
section <name>  (starts a group; tasks follow until the next section)
<task name>: <score>: <actor>[, <actor> ...]  (e.g. Make tea: 5: Me, Cat)
<task name>: <score>  (actors are optional)
score: number, intended range 1 (bad) to 5 (good)
notes: Detector is /^\s*journey/ (case-sensitive); the rest of the lexer is case-insensitive.
'#' starts a comment anywhere a token starts: text after '#' in a task, section or title is dropped.
';' in task names, section names or titles is a parse error. Task and section names cannot contain ':'.
A task whose name starts with 'section ' or 'title ' (any case) is read as that keyword and usually fails to parse.
The score is not validated: non-numbers become NaN, and values outside 1-5 render off the scale.
Indentation is free-form and has no meaning.
types.example:
journey
    title My working day
    section Go to work
      Make tea: 5: Me
      Go upstairs: 3: Me
      Do work: 1: Me, Cat
    section Go home
      Go downstairs: 5: Me
      Sit down: 5: Me

types.name: Timeline
types.purpose: Chronology: time periods in order, each with one or more events, optionally grouped into sections.
syntax: timeline [LR|TD]  (direction; LR is the default, TD is v11.14+)
title <text>
section <name>  (groups the following periods; all share a color)
<period> : <event>  (e.g. 2004 : Facebook)
<period> : <event> : <event>  (several events on one line)
: <event>  (continuation line: adds another event to the previous period)
<period>  (a period line with no events is allowed)
inside text forces a line break
notes: Detector is /^\s*timeline/ (case-sensitive); the rest of the lexer is case-insensitive.
An event starts at ':' followed by whitespace. Inside an event ':' is fine only if not followed by whitespace (Meet at 10:30 works).
Periods and section names cannot contain ':' at all: '10:30 : Standup' is a parse error. Quotes do not help; reword the period.
'#' at the start of a period begins a comment, and a period stops at '#'.
Only LR and TD are directions. 'timeline TB' parses but TB becomes a period named TB.
Period and event text is plain; no quoting syntax, no markdown strings.
types.example:
timeline
    title History of social media
    section 2002 - 2004
        2002 : LinkedIn
        2004 : Facebook : Google
    section 2005 - 2006
        2005 : YouTube
        2006 : Twitter
             : Meeting at 10:30

types.name: Mindmap
types.purpose: Hierarchical idea map radiating from a single root, with the tree defined by indentation.
syntax: <text>  (default shape; the text is also the id)
id[text]  (square)
id(text)  (rounded square)
id((text))  (circle)
id))text((  (bang)
id)text(  (cloud)
id{{text}}  (hexagon)
id["text with (parens) or [brackets]"]  (quoted text inside any shape)
id["`**bold** *italic* and a real newline`"]  (markdown string)
::icon(fa fa-book)  (own line after a node: icon for that node)
:::cls1 cls2  (own line after a node: CSS classes for that node)
blocks: Parent/child is defined only by indentation: a line indented deeper than the previous node is its child.
Exactly one root: the first node. Another node at or above the root's indentation throws 'There can be only one root'.
Uneven indentation: the parent is the nearest previous node with smaller indentation.
::icon() and ::: lines decorate the node just above them, regardless of their own indentation.
notes: Detector is /^\s*mindmap/ (case-sensitive).
Unquoted text containing ( ) [ ] { } is read as a shape: 'Foo (bar)' silently becomes id 'Foo ' with rounded text 'bar'. Quote it: a["Foo (bar)"].
No title, accTitle or accDescr statements: such lines just become nodes.
No edges or arrows; children are the only relation.
Icons need the icon font to be loaded by the host page; classes need CSS supplied by the host.

Use
for line breaks in plain text; markdown strings wrap automatically.
types.example:
mindmap
    root((mindmap))
        Origins
            Long history
            ::icon(fa fa-book)
            Popularisation
        Research
            id1[On effectiveness]
            id2("Automatic creation (tools)")
        Tools
            Pen and paper
            Mermaid

types.name: Kanban
types.purpose: Board of columns (workflow stages) holding task cards, with optional ticket, assignee and priority metadata.
syntax: colId[Column title]  (a column: node at the shallowest indentation)
itemId[Item text]  (an item: any node indented under a column)
[Text] or Text  (id is optional; a node without id gets a generated one)
itemId["Text with (parens)"]  (quote text containing brackets or parentheses)
itemId[Text]@{ ticket: MC-2037, assigned: 'knsv', priority: 'High' }  (metadata, same line, YAML-like)
metadata keys: assigned, ticket, priority, label, icon
priority values: 'Very High', 'High', 'Low', 'Very Low'
blocks: Columns are the nodes at the indentation of the first node; every deeper node is an item of the most recent column.
There is only one level of items: deeper indentation does not nest items inside items.
A node less indented than the first column throws 'Items without section detected'.
notes: Detector is /^\s*kanban/ (case-sensitive).
Unquoted text containing ( ) [ ] { } breaks parsing or becomes a shape; quote it: id["Fix (bug)"].
@{ ... } is parsed as YAML: quote values with spaces, commas or colons (priority: 'Very High').
Ticket links come from config kanban.ticketBaseUrl, with #TICKET# replaced by the ticket value.
Keep ids unique across the board (the docs' full example reuses id3).
No title, accTitle or accDescr statements; no edges.

types.name: Git graph
types.purpose: Git history: commits on branches, with branching, checkouts, merges and cherry-picks.
syntax: commit [id: "x"] [msg: "text" | "text"] [tag: "v1"] [type: NORMAL|REVERSE|HIGHLIGHT]  (attributes in any order)
branch <name> [order: <int>]  (creates the branch AND checks it out)
checkout <name>  |  switch <name>
merge <name> [id: "x"] [tag: "v1"] [type: ...]  (merges <name> into the current branch)
cherry-pick id: "x" [parent: "y"] [tag: "t"]
branch names: letters, digits, _ - . / (e.g. feature/login-v2), or a quoted string
starts on branch main (config gitGraph.mainBranchName changes it)
notes: Header is case-sensitive: gitgraph is not detected. A direction must be followed by a colon: 'gitGraph LR' is a parse error, use 'gitGraph LR:'.
id, msg, tag and parent values must be double- or single-quoted strings; id: abc is a parse error.
Attribute keywords are written with the colon attached: id: "a" or id:"a" work, id : "a" does not.
type values are uppercase only (HIGHLIGHT, not highlight).
merge has no msg attribute. Merging fails if the branch does not exist, has no commits, is the current branch, or has the same head as the current branch.
checkout of a branch never created is an error; branch with an existing name is an error.
cherry-pick needs an existing commit id from another branch, the current branch needs a commit, and a merge commit also needs parent: set to one of its parents.
Branch names that collide with keywords (commit, merge, ...) must be quoted.
types.example:
gitGraph
    commit id: "init"
    branch develop
    commit id: "feat-a"
    commit id: "feat-b" tag: "v0.1"
    checkout main
    commit id: "hotfix" type: HIGHLIGHT
    merge develop id: "merge-dev"
    branch release
    cherry-pick id: "feat-a"
    commit msg: "prepare release"

types.name: Quadrant chart
types.purpose: 2x2 matrix: points placed by two 0-1 scores on labeled axes, with a label per quadrant.
syntax: title <text>
x-axis <left text> [--> <right text>]  (e.g. x-axis Low Reach --> High Reach)
y-axis <bottom text> [--> <top text>]
quadrant-1 <text>  (top right); quadrant-2 top left; quadrant-3 bottom left; quadrant-4 bottom right
<point name>: [x, y]  (e.g. Campaign A: [0.3, 0.6])
<point name>: [x, y] radius: 12, color: #ff3300, stroke-color: #10f0f0, stroke-width: 5px  (inline style)
<point name>:::<class>: [x, y]  (e.g. Point A:::hot: [0.9, 0.1])
classDef <class> color: #109060, radius: 10, stroke-color: #310085, stroke-width: 10px
"quoted text" or "`markdown`" for any label containing other punctuation
notes: Detector is /^\s*quadrantChart/ (case-sensitive, camel case).
Coordinates must match 1 | 0 | 0.<digits>: 0.5, 0.0 and 1 work; 1.0, .5 and values > 1 are lexer errors.
Unquoted labels allow letters, digits, spaces and - _ . , & + = * # / ! ? etc. but not ( ) [ ] or ':'; quote such labels: "Item (x)": [0.5, 0.5].
A line starting with title (any case), even inside a point name, is taken as the title: 'Title page: [0.5, 0.5]' silently becomes a title.
x-axis/y-axis with only the first text and a trailing --> gets an arrow appended to that text.
';' can end a statement like a newline.
types.example:
quadrantChart
    title Reach and engagement of campaigns
    x-axis Low Reach --> High Reach
    y-axis Low Engagement --> High Engagement
    quadrant-1 We should expand
    quadrant-2 Need to promote
    quadrant-3 Re-evaluate
    quadrant-4 May be improved
    Campaign A: [0.3, 0.6]
    Campaign B: [0.45, 0.23] radius: 10, color: #ff3300
    Campaign C:::hot: [0.78, 0.9]
    "Campaign D (pilot)": [0.1, 0]
    classDef hot color: #d62728, radius: 12

types.name: XY chart
types.purpose: Bar and line charts over a categorical or numeric x-axis and a numeric y-axis.
syntax: xychart [horizontal|vertical]  (orientation; vertical is the default)
title "Chart title"
x-axis ["title"] [cat1, "cat 2", cat3]  (categorical)
x-axis ["title"] <min> --> <max>  (numeric range)
y-axis ["title"] [<min> --> <max>]  (numeric only; range auto-computed if omitted)
bar ["series name"] [n1, n2, ...]  (e.g. bar "Revenue" [5000, 6000, 7500])
line ["series name"] [n1, n2, ...]
numbers: optional sign, decimals, leading-dot allowed (+1.3, -3.4, .98)
per-point label (grammar only, undocumented): line [10 "Start", 20, 30 "End"]
named series appear in the legend (v11.17+); unnamed ones do not
notes: xychart and xychart-beta are both accepted (detector /^\s*xychart(-beta)?/); prefer xychart. Detection is case-sensitive.
Quote every text with spaces: whitespace between unquoted words is dropped, so title Sales Revenue renders as SalesRevenue.
Unquoted words equal to keywords (line, bar, title, x-axis, y-axis, horizontal, vertical) are parse errors in labels; quote them.
Unquoted text allows only ASCII letters, digits and & + = * # . - _; anything else (non-ASCII such as CJK, parentheses, $, %, :, /) needs quotes.
Each series should have one value per x-axis category.
The y-axis cannot be categorical; there is no scatter, area or stacked type.
';' can end a statement like a newline.
types.example:
xychart
    title "Sales Revenue"
    x-axis "Month" [jan, feb, mar, apr, may, jun]
    y-axis "Revenue (in $)" 4000 --> 11000
    bar "Actual" [5000, 6000, 7500, 8200, 9500, 10500]
    line "Target" [5500, 6500, 7000, 8000, 9000, 10000]

types.name: Sankey
types.purpose: Show weighted flows between nodes (energy, money, traffic) as bands whose width is the flow value.
syntax: header alone on line 1, then CSV rows: sankey
source,target,value  e.g. Coal,Electricity grid,63.9
value is a number parsed with parseFloat, e.g. 35 or 0.597
field with a comma: wrap in double quotes  e.g. Gas,"Heating, homes",12
double quote inside a quoted field: double it  e.g. "The ""big"" one",Sink,5
a node is created implicitly by its first appearance as source or target
blank lines between rows are allowed and ignored
relations: each row is one directed link source -> target with width = value
notes: Exactly 3 columns per row; no header row (a 'source,target,value' line would become a link with NaN value).
Only single quotes are literal text; double quotes start a CSV-quoted field.
Grammar lexer accepts only printable ASCII (U+0020-U+007E) in fields, quoted or not; non-ASCII names (CJK, accents, emoji) fail to lex.
Leading/trailing spaces on each row are trimmed; spaces inside names are kept.
%% after data on a row is not a comment (it is field text); whole-line %% comments are removed by Mermaid before parsing.
Links must not form a cycle (d3-sankey cannot lay out circular links).
No styling, classes, or per-link colors in the source; use config sankey.linkColor / nodeAlignment / showValues.
types.example:
sankey
Solar,Grid,60
Wind,Grid,290
Coal,Grid,120
Grid,Homes,210
Grid,"Industry, heavy",180
Grid,Losses,80

types.name: Packet
types.purpose: Draw the bit layout of a network packet or register as rows of labeled bit fields.
syntax: start-end: "label"  e.g. 0-15: "Source Port"
start: "label"  single bit, e.g. 106: "URG"
+bits: "label"  width only, starts after previous field, e.g. +16: "Length"
forms can be mixed: +16: "A" then 16-31: "B"
title Text  e.g. title UDP Packet
label is a quoted string, double or single quotes: 8: 'flag'
trailing %% comment after a field is allowed
notes: Fields must be contiguous from bit 0 in ascending order: no gaps, no overlaps (error 'not contiguous').
Ranges are always low-high (0-7); 7-0 is an error. Draw MSB-left with config packet.bitOrder: descending.
+0 is an error (zero bit field); end must be >= start.
Unquoted labels are not allowed.
Fields wider than bitsPerRow (default 32) wrap across rows automatically.
Only integer bit numbers; no hex (0x10) or negative values.
types.example:
packet
title UDP Packet
+16: "Source Port"
+16: "Destination Port"
32-47: "Length"
48-63: "Checksum"
64-95: "Data (variable length)"

types.name: Block
types.purpose: Lay out blocks on an author-controlled column grid (system/component layouts) with optional edges.
syntax: columns N | columns auto  e.g. columns 3
id  plain block labeled with its id; several per line: a b c
id["label"]  rectangle; label must be double-quoted
shapes: id("..") round, id([".."]) stadium, id[[".."]] subroutine, id[("..")] cylinder
shapes: id(("..")) circle, id(((".."))) double circle, id>".."] asymmetric, id{".."} rhombus, id{{".."}} hexagon
shapes: id[/".."/] parallelogram, id[\".."\] alt parallelogram, id[/".."\] trapezoid, id[\".."/] alt trapezoid
id:N  span N columns, e.g. b:2 or a["A"]:2
space | space:N  empty cell(s), e.g. space:2
id<["label"]>(dir)  block arrow; dir: right left up down x y, e.g. ar<["go"]>(x, down)
classDef name css  e.g. classDef hot fill:#f96,stroke:#333
class id1,id2 name  e.g. class a,b hot
style id css  e.g. style a fill:#969,stroke-width:4px
relations: A --> B arrow; A --- B line; A ==> B thick; A -.-> B dotted
A --x B cross end; A --o B circle end; A <--> B both ends
A -- "label" --> B  labeled edge
blocks: block:id ... end  named composite block; block:id:N ... end spans N columns
block ... end  anonymous composite block
composites nest; each has its own 'columns' setting; indentation is cosmetic
notes: Shape labels must be double-quoted: a[Label] fails, write a["Label"]. Single quotes are not strings.
Node ids cannot contain - ( ) [ ] { } < > : = or whitespace.
Reserved whole words (not usable as ids): block, end, space, columns, default, class, style, classDef, linkStyle, interpolate.
Every block / block:id needs a matching end.
Without 'columns', all children of a level are placed in one row (columns auto).
Layout is the grid order of declaration; there is no direction keyword (no TD/LR).
types.example:
block
    columns 3
    a["Frontend"] b:2
    block:svc:3
        columns 2
        api("API") db[("DB")]
    end
    space
    arr<["sync"]>(down)
    c{"Check"}
    a --> api
    api -- "query" --> db
    classDef hot fill:#f96,stroke:#333
    class c hot

types.name: Architecture
types.purpose: Show cloud/CI services, their groups, and how they connect, with icons and side-anchored edges.
syntax: group id(icon)[Title] (in parentId)?  e.g. group api(cloud)[API]
service id(icon)[Title] (in groupId)?  e.g. service db(database)[Database] in api
icon and title are optional: service s1, service s2[Only Title]
junction id (in groupId)?  4-way split point, e.g. junction j1 in api
edge: a:SIDE -- SIDE:b  SIDE is L R T B, e.g. db:R -- L:server
arrowheads: a:R --> L:b, a:R <-- L:b, a:R <--> L:b
edge out of a group: a{group}:B --> T:b{group}
align row id1 id2 ...  same y; align column id1 id2 ... same x (2+ members)
title Text
relations: -- plain edge; < before and/or > after the dashes adds arrowheads
-[label]- edge with a label, e.g. a:R -[HTTP]-> L:b (in grammar, not in docs; parses in 12.1.0)
blocks: nesting is declared with 'in parentId', not by indentation or end
notes: Header must be architecture-beta. The 12.1.0 detector also matches plain 'architecture', but the Langium grammar only accepts 'architecture-beta', so plain fails to parse.
Built-in icons: cloud, database, disk, internet, server. Others need a registered icon pack: (logos:aws-s3); this editor has logos, mdi, fa, fas, far, fab.
Sides are uppercase L R T B only; ids named L, R, T or B, or keywords (group, service, junction, in, align, row, column), break lexing.
Ids: word chars and inner dashes (my-db ok, trailing dash not). Declare ids before referencing them.
Title [..] cannot contain [ or ] unless quoted inside: ["a [b]"].
{group} modifier only works on services that are inside a group; group ids themselves cannot be edge endpoints.
align order must not contradict edge sides, or layout fails.
types.example:
architecture-beta
    group cloud_grp(cloud)[Cloud]
    group data(database)[Data] in cloud_grp
    service api(server)[API] in cloud_grp
    service db(database)[Primary DB] in data
    service cache(disk)[Cache] in data
    service users(internet)[Users]
    junction hub in cloud_grp
    users:R --> L:api
    api:B -- T:hub
    hub:L -- R:db
    hub:R -- L:cache

types.name: Radar
types.purpose: Compare several entities across multiple numeric dimensions on a circular (spider) chart.
syntax: axis id["Label"], id2["Label"]  e.g. axis m["Math"], s["Science"] (label optional: axis A, B, C)
multiple axis lines accumulate in order
curve id["Label"]{v1, v2, ...}  values in axis order, e.g. curve a["Alice"]{85, 90, 80}
curve id{axisId: v, ...}  keyed values, e.g. curve b{ m: 70, s: 75 }
several curves per line: curve x{1,2,3}, y{3,2,1}
max N / min N  scale bounds, e.g. max 100
ticks N  number of graticule rings, e.g. ticks 5
graticule circle | graticule polygon
showLegend true | showLegend false
title Text
notes: Header must be radar-beta (radar-beta: also accepted by grammar); plain 'radar' is not detected in 12.1.0.
Labels go in ["..."] and must be quoted strings.
Values are non-negative numbers only (no minus sign in the NUMBER terminal).
A curve uses either all plain numbers or all axis:value pairs, not a mix.
Ids cannot be keywords: axis, curve, max, min, ticks, graticule, showLegend, true, false, circle, polygon.
Option keywords are case-sensitive (showLegend, not showlegend).
types.example:
radar-beta
    title Team Skills
    axis fe["Frontend"], be["Backend"], ops["DevOps"]
    axis ux["UX"], qa["Testing"]
    curve alice["Alice"]{4, 3, 2, 5, 3}
    curve bob["Bob"]{ fe: 2, be: 5, ops: 4, ux: 1, qa: 4 }
    max 5
    min 0
    ticks 5
    graticule polygon
    showLegend true

types.name: Treemap
types.purpose: Show hierarchical data as nested rectangles sized by value.
syntax: "Section"  parent node (no value), e.g. "Products"
"Leaf": value  leaf node, e.g. "Phones": 50
"Leaf", value  comma separator also accepted by grammar
"Name":::className  class on a section; "Leaf": 20:::className on a leaf
classDef name css  e.g. classDef hot fill:#f96,stroke:#333
names may use double or single quotes, e.g. 'Item A'; a name cannot contain its own quote char (use "Men's")
title Text
blocks: hierarchy by indentation (spaces or tabs); deeper indent = child of the nearest less-indented line above
notes: All node names must be quoted; bare names fail.
Values are non-negative numbers (digits, '.', '_' or ','); no minus sign.
A section's size is the sum of its leaves; do not give sections a value.
Several unindented top-level sections are allowed (the single-root validator in the parser package is not enforced by mermaid.parse).
Trailing whitespace after a row is a parse error (indentation tokens are significant); keep indentation consistent.
Only %% comments; no edges or links.
Number formatting is config (treemap.valueFormat), not syntax.
types.example:
treemap
"Budget"
    "Operations"
        "Salaries": 700
        "Equipment": 200:::hot
    "Marketing"
        "Ads": 400
        "Events": 100
classDef hot fill:#f96,stroke:#333

types.name: Tree view
types.purpose: Render a directory-like tree (file trees, hierarchies) with connector lines and optional icons/annotations.
syntax: one node per line; depth = indentation, e.g. src/ then indented index.js
bare label: index.js, my-project/, emoji and spaces allowed (🚀 rocket-app/)
quoted label: "my file.txt" or 'my file.txt' (optional; bare labels may contain spaces)
trailing / marks a directory (bold): src/
Name :::className  CSS class, built-in: :::highlight
Name icon(pack:name)  per-node icon, e.g. icon(logos:react); icon() or icon(none) hides it
Name ## text  inline description, e.g. index.ts ## entry point
annotations combine in any order: App.tsx :::highlight icon(logos:react) ## main
box-drawing input auto-detected: ├── src/  │   └── a.ts  └── README.md (also heavy ┣━━ ┗━━ ┃)
title Text  (only before the first node)
blocks: nesting purely by indentation (spaces; tabs expanded) or by box-drawing column position
notes: Header is case-sensitive treeView-beta; plain 'treeView' and 'treeview-beta' are not detected in 12.1.0.
Annotations need whitespace before them: 'a.ts :::x', not 'a.ts:::x'.
Description after ## runs to end of line; # alone is plain label text.
No edges, no ids, no classDef statement (only :::class referencing built-in or themed classes).
Icons are hidden by default (config treeView.showIcons); icon() packs must be registered by the host, else a ? renders (this editor has logos, mdi, fa, fas, far, fab).
title / accTitle / accDescr must come before the first node.
types.example:
treeView-beta
title Repository layout
    my-app/
        src/
            App.tsx :::highlight ## main component
            index.ts ## entry point
        tests/
            app.test.ts
        package.json
        "read me.md"

types.name: Event modeling
types.purpose: Model a system as a timeline of UI, commands, events, read models and processors in swimlanes (Event Modeling method).
syntax: tf NN type Entity  time frame, e.g. tf 01 ui CartUI (relaxed: timeframe 01 ui CartUI)
rf NN type Entity  reset frame: no inferred link from the previous frame (relaxed: resetframe)
types: ui, cmd|command, evt|event, rmo|readmodel, pcr|processor
NN = 1-3 digits, unique across all tf/rf, e.g. 01, 102
Namespace.Entity  qualified name makes its own swimlane, e.g. evt Inventory.Changed
explicit sources: tf 05 rmo Cart ->> 02 ->> 03
inline data on the frame line: tf 02 cmd AddItem { price: number }
data reference: tf 02 cmd AddItem [[AddItem01]]
data block: data AddItem01 { NEWLINE ... NEWLINE }  (closing } at column 0)
optional data type: `json`{ "a": 1 }; types json jsobj figma salt uri md html text
title Text
relations: frames are linked automatically in timeline order (inferred)
->> NN  adds an explicit link from frame NN; rf stops the inferred link
notes: Header is exactly 'eventmodeling' (lowercase, no -beta); this diagram never had a beta keyword.
Duplicate frame numbers are an error; '01' and '1' are different frame names.
data blocks must span lines: '{' then newline, content, and '}' at the start of its own line. A one-line 'data X { ... }' fails.
Comments: %% plus // line and /* */ block comments are accepted.
Grammar also accepts 'entity Name', 'note NN {block}', and 'gwt NN given ... when ... then ...', but 12.1.0 docs do not cover them and the renderer ignores them.
Keywords (tf, rf, data, note, entity, gwt, and type names) cannot be used as entity names.
types.example:
eventmodeling
tf 01 ui CartUI
tf 02 cmd AddItem [[AddItem01]]
tf 03 evt ItemAdded { description: string }
tf 04 rmo CartItems
rf 05 evt Inventory.StockChanged
tf 06 pcr StockProcessor ->> 05
tf 07 cmd ReserveStock
data AddItem01 {
  description: 'john'
  price: 20.4
}

types.name: Ishikawa
types.purpose: Fishbone (cause-and-effect) diagram: a problem at the head with categorized causes on the bones.
syntax: first line after the header = the effect/problem, e.g. Blurry Photo
each following line = one cause, plain text, e.g. Process
indent deeper to nest sub-causes under the cause above
the effect may also be indented; depth is measured relative to the first cause
blocks: hierarchy only by indentation; no braces or end
notes: The whole trimmed line is the label: no ids, shapes, quotes, classes or edges.
Header is case-insensitive (Ishikawa works); -beta is optional in 12.1.0 (docs still show ishikawa-beta).
A cause line starting with the word 'ishikawa' is lexed as the header keyword and breaks parsing.
Top-level causes become the main bones (categories); their children are sub-causes.
Whole-line %% comments are allowed.
types.example:
ishikawa
    Blurry Photo
    Process
        Out of focus
        Shutter speed too slow
    User
        Shaky hands
    Equipment
        Lens
            Dirty lens
            Damaged lens
    Environment
        Too dark

types.name: Venn
types.purpose: Overlapping circles showing sets and their intersections, with optional sizes and text items inside regions.
syntax: title Text  (rest of line; stops at # or ;)
set ID  e.g. set Frontend
set ID["Label"]  e.g. set A["Alpha"]  (also unquoted set A[Alpha])
set ID:N / set ID["Label"]:N  size suffix, e.g. set A["Alpha"]:20
union ID,ID[,ID...]["Label"][:N]  e.g. union A,B["Shared"]:3
ID is a bare word [A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_-]* or a quoted string, e.g. set "Foo Bar"
indented text under a set/union attaches to it: text TID["Label"], text "free text", text 42
unindented form names the target sets: text A,B TID["Label"]
style ID[,ID...] prop:value[, prop:value]  e.g. style A fill:#ff6b6b, fill-opacity:0.3
style props: fill, color, stroke, stroke-width, fill-opacity; targets may be sets, unions (by their ids) or text ids
blocks: No braces/end; a text line indented below a set or union line belongs to the most recent set/union.
notes: Header must be exactly lowercase venn-beta (detector is case-sensitive); statement keywords themselves are case-insensitive.
Every id in a union must be declared earlier with set, otherwise: unknown set identifier.
union needs at least two ids; ids are comma-separated with no brackets around the list.

If the body is indented, any indented line starting with text after a set/union is parsed as the attached form, so text A,B TID[...] fails there; put text lines directly under their set/union instead.
Labels go in ["..."] right after the id, before the :N size; no quotes inside a label.
No arrows, no classDef/:::, no inline colors on set lines; color only via style lines.
types.example:
venn-beta
    title Skills
    set A["Frontend"]:20
        text A1["React"]
    set B["Backend"]:12
        text B1["API"]
    union A,B["Shared"]:3
        text AB1["OpenAPI"]
    style A fill:#ff6b6b
    style A,B color:#333

types.name: Use case
types.purpose: UML use case diagram: actors, use cases, system boundaries and their associations, include/extend and generalization.
syntax: direction LR  (TD, TB, BT, LR, RL)
actor ID / actor ID("Label")  e.g. actor Admin("Main administrator")
actor ID@{ type: hollow }  (type: hollow|awesome, icon: "fa:user", business: true)
ID("Label") ellipse use case, ID[Label] rectangle use case, bare ID or "Quoted name" also declares one
suffix order: ID(label)@{ ... } <<Stereotype>>:::class  e.g. Quote("Prepare quote")@{ business: true } <<Core>>
systemBoundary ID["Title"]@{ type: package }:::cls ... end  (type rect default, or package)
note for TARGET "text"  (one actor or use case)
json ID@{ "key": "value", "n": 3 }:::cls  (strict JSON object, top level only)
edge id and label: A e1@-- "label" ---> B  then e1@{ animation: fast } / e1@{ animate: false }
classDef name prop:val,prop:val / class ID1,ID2 name / style ID prop:val
labels: unquoted text, "plain string", or "`markdown string`" (may span lines)
relations: A --> B / A <-- B / A -- B  solid association (point, reversed, markerless); more dashes = longer edge (A ---> B)
A --o B / B o-- A / A --x B / B x-- A  circle / cross association ends
A -- "label" --> B  labelled association (label between the dashes)
A ..> : include B  source use case includes target
A ..> : extend B  source use case extends base B
A --|> B  generalization (actor to actor or use case to use case)
blocks: systemBoundary ... end: one level only; inside may be only actor and use case declarations, blank lines and %% comments.
Relationships, notes, json, direction, class/style lines must be at top level (outside boundaries).
notes: Header is exactly lowercase usecase-beta; there is no title keyword (title Foo is a parse error) - use front matter title or accTitle.
Actors must be declared with actor ID somewhere; undeclared endpoints become ellipse use cases. There is no usecase keyword.
One statement per physical line; no ; separators. Ids match [A-Za-z0-9_]+ and are diagram-wide.
Not supported (PlantUML habits): actor A as "X", :Actor:, -> arrows, ..> without : include/extend, A --> B : label, package/rectangle blocks, skinparam, left/right/up/down hints, note left of.
include/extend are case-insensitive words after ..> :; a label containing include on a --> edge stays an ordinary association.
Reserved words cannot be ids: actor, end, note, for, json, class, classDef, style, direction, systemBoundary, TD/TB/BT/LR/RL, true, false.
Plain strings do not process \n escapes; use a markdown string with a real newline or #quot; / #40; entity codes.
style values: comma-separated prop:val, no semicolons; use \, for a literal comma.
types.example:
usecase-beta
direction LR
actor Customer
actor Staff("Order staff")@{ type: hollow }
systemBoundary shop["Online shop"]@{ type: package }
    Browse("Browse products")
    Checkout("Checkout") <<Core>>
    Payment("Process payment")
    Review[Review order]
end
note for Checkout "Validates the cart"
Customer --> Browse
Customer c1@-- "places order" ---> Checkout
Checkout ..> : include Payment
Staff --> Review
Staff --|> Customer
classDef core stroke:#c33,stroke-width:2px
class Checkout core
c1@{ animation: fast }

types.name: Wardley map
types.purpose: Wardley map: components of a value chain positioned by visibility (y) and evolution (x), with dependencies and evolution moves.
syntax: title Text / size [1100, 600]  (size takes integers)
anchor Name [visibility, evolution]  e.g. anchor Customer [0.90, 0.95]
component Name [vis, evo]  e.g. component Hot Water [0.52, 0.80]
component Name [vis, evo] label [-60, 10] (build|buy|outsource|market) (inertia)  (each suffix optional, in this order; inertia may be bare)
evolve Name 0.75  (target evolution)
evolution Genesis -> Custom -> Product -> Commodity  (stage labels; Stage@0.25 sets boundary, Stage / Alt for dual label)
pipeline Parent { NEWLINE component Name [0.4] ... }  (single evolution value per child)
note "text" [vis, evo]  (text must be quoted)
annotations [0.10, 0.90] / annotation 1,[0.60, 0.65] "text"
accelerator Name [x, y] / deaccelerator Name [x, y]
Names: unquoted words with spaces/hyphens/()& allowed if starting with a letter; otherwise "quoted"
relations: A -> B  dependency (also A --> B, A > B)
A -.-> B  dashed link
A +> B / A +< B / A +<> B  flow forward / reverse / both
A +'label'> B  labelled flow (also +'label'< and +'label'<>)
A -> B; annotation text  link label after ;
blocks: pipeline Parent { ... } : opening { on the pipeline line, each child component on its own line, closing } on its own line.
notes: Header must be lowercase wardley-beta; the detector is case-insensitive but the parser rejects WARDLEY-BETA.
Coordinates are [visibility, evolution] (y first, then x), each a decimal 0.0-1.0; integers like 1 or 0 are rejected (write 1.0 / 0.0).
Names starting with a digit or other non-letter must be quoted ("3D Printer"); a quoted name is referenced quoted too.
Trend syntax from the docs (A -.- (x, y)) is NOT in the 12.1.0 grammar and fails to parse.
Every link needs an arrow; two names with no arrow merge into one name and fail.
Keywords are lowercase reserved words: component, anchor, evolve, evolution, pipeline, note, annotation(s), accelerator, deaccelerator, size, label, inertia.
No classDef/style; handDrawn look not supported.
types.example:
wardley-beta
title Tea Shop
evolution Genesis@0.25 -> Custom@0.5 -> Product@0.75 -> Commodity@1.0
anchor Business [0.95, 0.63]
component Cup of Tea [0.79, 0.61]
component Tea [0.63, 0.81] (buy)
component Hot Water [0.52, 0.80]
component Kettle [0.43, 0.35] (build) (inertia)
component Power [0.10, 0.70] (market)
Business -> Cup of Tea
Cup of Tea -> Tea
Cup of Tea -> Hot Water
Hot Water +> Kettle
Kettle -> Power; electricity
evolve Kettle 0.62
pipeline Kettle {
    component Electric [0.55]
    component Stovetop [0.30]
}
note "Standard power lets kettles evolve" [0.30, 0.49]
annotations [0.10, 0.90]
annotation 1,[0.43, 0.35] "Inertia here"

types.name: Cynefin
types.purpose: Cynefin sense-making framework: items placed in the five fixed domains, with transitions between domains.
syntax: title Text  (optional)
complex | complicated | clear | chaotic | confusion  opens that domain's block
"Item label"  quoted item on following lines under a domain (single quotes also accepted)
domain with no items is allowed (renders empty)
FROM --> TO  transition between two domains, e.g. clear --> chaotic
FROM --> TO : "Label"  labelled transition (label must be quoted)
relations: complex --> complicated : "Pattern identified"  only operator is -->, both ends must be domain keywords
blocks: A domain block is the domain keyword followed by quoted items; it ends at the next domain keyword or transition. Indentation is optional and not significant.
notes: Header must be lowercase cynefin-beta (optionally cynefin-beta:); Cynefin-beta is not detected.
Domain names are fixed lowercase keywords; Complex, disorder, obvious, simple are rejected.
Items must be quoted strings; unquoted item text is a lexer error.
Transition labels must be quoted; complex --> clear : Pattern fails.
Self-loop transitions (complex --> complex) are ignored; domain placement is fixed regardless of order.
confusion shows at most 3 items (+N more badge); no styling, classes, or handDrawn look.
types.example:
cynefin-beta
    title Incident Response
    complex
        "Investigate root cause"
    complicated
        "Analyze performance data"
    clear
        "Restart service"
    chaotic
        "Page on-call immediately"
    confusion
        "Unknown failure mode"
    complex --> complicated : "Pattern identified"
    clear --> chaotic : "Complacency"

types.name: Railroad
types.purpose: Railroad (syntax) diagram written directly in Mermaid's railroad IR as explicit constructor calls.
syntax: title Text  (optional; surrounding quotes are stripped)
rule_name = EXPR ;  every rule ends with ;
terminal("text")  literal
nonterminal("name")  rule reference (argument is a quoted string)
sequence(a, b, ...)  elements in order
choice(a, b, ...)  alternatives
optional(a) / zeroOrMore(a) / oneOrMore(a)  single argument
special("text")  special sequence box
rule names: [A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_-]*; strings "..." or '...'
blocks: Constructors nest freely; whitespace and newlines are insignificant, so a rule may span many lines until its ;.
notes: Header must be lowercase railroad-beta (detector is case-insensitive, parser is not).
Every terminal/nonterminal must use a constructor: bare "x" or bare names inside an expression are errors, and nonterminal(term) without quotes fails.
Juxtaposition is not a sequence: terminal("a") terminal("b") fails; wrap in sequence(...).
Comments: %% line comments and /* block */ comments.
title/accTitle/accDescr must come before the first rule.
Use railroad-ebnf-beta / -abnf-beta / -peg-beta for grammar notations; this type accepts only constructors.

types.name: Railroad (EBNF)
types.purpose: Railroad (syntax) diagram generated from grammar rules written in EBNF (W3C or ISO 14977 style).
syntax: title Text  (optional; surrounding quotes are stripped)
name = definition ;  or  name ::= definition ;  (every rule ends with ;)
"text" or 'text'  terminal; bare name  nonterminal reference
A B  or  A , B  sequence (comma optional)
A | B  choice
A?  [ A ]  optional
A*  { A }  zero or more;  A+  one or more
( A | B )  grouping
A - B  exception (needs spaces around -)
? description ?  special sequence
names: [A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_-]*
relations: = / ::=  rule definition;  |  alternation;  ,  optional sequence separator
notes: Header must be lowercase railroad-ebnf-beta (detector is case-insensitive, parser is not).
Missing final ; is a parse error; rules may span lines.
- is a name character: a-b is ONE nonterminal named a-b; write a - b for exception.
No character classes: [a-z] parses as an optional nonterminal named a-z, not a range. Spell out terminals.
Comments: (* iso *), /* w3c */ and %% lines. # and // are not comments.
title/accTitle/accDescr must come before the first rule.
No repetition counts (3 * A) or BNF <angle> names.

types.name: Railroad (ABNF)
types.purpose: Railroad (syntax) diagram generated from grammar rules written in ABNF (RFC 5234 style).
syntax: title Text  (optional; surrounding quotes are stripped)
name = elements ;  every rule ends with ; (unlike RFC 5234)
A B  concatenation (whitespace)
A / B  alternation
( A B )  group;  [ A ]  optional
*A  zero or more;  1*A  one or more;  2*4A  between 2 and 4;  3A  exactly 3
"text"  terminal (double quotes only)
%x41 / %d65 / %b1000001  numeric values; ranges %x30-39; concatenation %x0D.0A
rule names: [A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9-]*  e.g. local-part, ALPHA, DIGIT (core rules are just names)
relations: =  rule definition;  /  alternation
notes: Header must be lowercase railroad-abnf-beta (detector is case-insensitive, parser is not).
; both ends a rule and starts a comment: a trailing comment after a rule (a = "x" ; note) swallows the terminator and breaks parsing. Put ; comments on their own line.
Single-quoted strings 'x' are lexer errors; use "x" or %x values.
Not supported: =/ incremental alternatives, <prose-val>, %s/%i case modifiers, rules without a trailing ;.
Rule names cannot contain _ and must start with a letter.
title/accTitle/accDescr must come before the first rule.

types.name: Railroad (PEG)
types.purpose: Railroad (syntax) diagram generated from grammar rules written as a Parsing Expression Grammar.
syntax: title Text  (optional; surrounding quotes are stripped)
Name <- expression ;  every rule ends with ;
A B  sequence (whitespace)
A / B  ordered choice
A?  A*  A+  optional / zero or more / one or more (suffix)
&A  and-predicate;  !A  not-predicate (prefix)
( A / B )  grouping
.  any single character
"text" or 'text'  literal; bare Name  rule reference
names: [A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_-]*
relations: <-  rule definition;  /  ordered choice
notes: Header must be lowercase railroad-peg-beta (detector is case-insensitive, parser is not).
Definition operator is <- only; = or <-- fail.
No character classes: [a-z] is a lexer error; spell out literals with /.
Comments: # to end of line, and %% lines.
Missing final ; is a parse error; rules may span lines.
title/accTitle/accDescr must come before the first rule.

types.name: Info
types.purpose: Diagnostic diagram that renders the running Mermaid version; no user content.
syntax: info  (the whole diagram can be just this keyword)
info showInfo  (optional showInfo flag, same line or a following line)
title Text / accTitle: Text / accDescr: Text  (optional, after info/showInfo)
notes: Keyword is lowercase and case-sensitive: INFO or Info is not detected.
Nothing else is accepted: any other word (e.g. info version, info foo) is a lexer error.
No -beta suffix; there is no doc page for this type, it is a debugging aid rather than a real diagram.
types.example:
info
showInfo
